LIVE: `DIFF fn_800C03E0 insns 433/433 lines 568 real 508`, and the raw read is `433 insns, DIFFERING WORDS = 216, MNEMONIC DIVERGENCE = 0, PINNED = no`, all 216 REGFIELD-ONLY. Trigger FIRED. DISPOSITION: mark v1 superseded by v2 explicitly -- the supersession is true in fact and unrecorded, which is why the expired v1 still answers queries. attributes.tooling_gap: `gdlmem stale` CANNOT SEE AN EXPIRED DENIAL, and this is the reason five records with fired triggers stayed live for a day and needed a hand sweep to find. Measured: `python memory_graph/gdlmem.py stale` at c0f978273 returns the keys active_work_claims (6), missing_from_report (2), multi_record_functions (208), postprocessor_walls (101), reopen_candidates (14), stale_solved (15), suspect_low_fuzzy (0), valid_count (201) -- there is NO denial or expiry dimension, and its own `note` field does not mention denials. NONE of the five appears in stale_solved (whose 15 rows are all fuzzy-100 functions) or in reopen_candidates (14 rows, none of them these). The only one of the six that `stale` mentions at all is MBCameraUpdate, and it appears under `postprocessor_walls` via the OTHER record (attempt.CL_mbcameraupdate-frame-40-...v2), classified as a VALID source-level wall -- which is right for v2 and says nothing about v1's expiry. THE ASK, for T22: `stale` already walks every accepted record for `anchor_path_missing`; the same walk can evaluate `denial.expiry_check` triggers that are MECHANICAL (a quoted number against a live wf_word_diff / fndiff read) and emit an `expired_denials` bucket. The population it would have caught today is six, of which two (the CritterGetTargetPlayers pair) are ALSO in the vacuous class, so the two screens compose rather than duplicate.
